assumptions: The null named (base composition, k-let shuffles, or R'MES's maximal-order Markov model) is what 'expected' means; a finding is relative to it.
Sites are NEB's exact recognition sequences; degenerate sites are not swept.
limits: Avoidance is evidence of a lineage's restriction-modification history, not proof of it.
Short sequences give little power for long sites.
bio.jane/contract.question: Which exact restriction sites does each sequence carry far less, or far more, often than a stated null predicts?

description: Sweep a set of sequences against every exact recognition site in the NEB catalog and report the sites each one carries far less (avoided) or far more (enriched) often than a stated null predicts, with the false discovery rate controlled across every (sequence, site) test. Avoidance is evidence of the restriction–modification systems a lineage has lived with, and a site a design can rely on being rare. Three nulls: base composition (order-0, Poisson); k-let-preserving shuffles (uShuffle), which holds dinucleotide skews such as CpG depletion in the null rather than reporting them as findings; and R'MES's maximal-order Markov model, the standard in published avoidance analyses, which judges a site of length k against the record's own (k−1)-mers so only what those cannot explain is reported.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

alpha.description: false discovery rate at which a site is reported avoided or enriched.

correction.description: Benjamini–Hochberg (independent or positively dependent tests) or Benjamini–Yekutieli (any dependence, including overlapping sites on one sequence; less power). Values: BH (Benjamini–Hochberg), BY (Benjamini–Yekutieli).

enzymes.description: restrict the sweep to these enzymes' sites (NEB names). Empty sweeps every exact site in the catalog; degenerate (IUPAC) sites are never swept and are listed in the result. Advanced.

include_subject.description: also sweep the node's subject (the open or wired record).

min_site_length.description: shortest recognition site swept. In bp.

null_model.description: what a site is rare relative to: base composition, shuffles that keep the record's own k-let counts, or the record's own (k−1)-mers for a site of length k (R'MES maximal order, Gaussian score). Values: order0 (Base composition (order-0)), shuffle (k-let shuffles (uShuffle)), maximal (Maximal-order Markov (R'MES)).

positions.description: also return every occurrence's coordinate and strand, for drawing on a map. Advanced.

seed.description: seed for the shuffles, so a run reproduces. Only applies when null_model is shuffle. Advanced.

sequences.description: the corpus: wire upstream records here, or list library document names. Each is one record of the sweep.

shuffle_k.description: k-let size the shuffles preserve. 2 holds every dinucleotide count, so CpG depletion is in the null. Only applies when null_model is shuffle.

shuffles.description: shuffles per record. The smallest p the null can give is 1 / (shuffles + 1). Only applies when null_model is shuffle.

name: discover_site_avoidance

avoided.description: tests whose low-tail q is at or below alpha, most extreme ratio first

avoidedCount.description: how many (record, site) tests were called avoided

correction.description: the multiple-testing correction that ran, and why it is valid

enriched.description: tests whose high-tail q is at or below alpha, most extreme ratio first

enrichedCount.description: how many (record, site) tests were called enriched

nullModel.description: the null the p-values stand on, stated with every run

sweep.description: the full result, including the records swept and the degenerate sites skipped

tests.description: every (record, site) test: observed, expected, ratio, both tails and both q-values; under the maximal-order null also the R'MES score z and its variance
